Here are a few key ideas from his thought:

Locke believed that human beings were born with an infinite capacity to reason and have certain innate rights, including the right to life and freedom.  He believed that human beings have a natural tendency to make rational judgments about the world, and that knowledge comes from reason.  He also held that there is no such thing as a bad action.  His view is often contrasted with the idea of natural evil, which is the idea that humans are faced with certain bad events in the world, in particular natural disasters, that are caused by supernatural forces.  Locke did not believe in an all-powerful God who controls certain events, but he believed in the idea that humans are capable of reason, and can make decisions about what actions to take in the face of certain events.  Locke also believed that it was impossible to be free from certain evils that existed in the world.  There is no guarantee of safety, and there will always be some degree of suffering in the world.  Locke argued in favor of certain positive freedoms in order to prevent a situation where people are unable to make choices, which would be a sad state of affairs.  He believed in the concept of an “inalienable moral right of each person to life, liberty, and property” which he claimed could never be taken away from him.
